extraction_scope: Worker-6 adjudicated mechanism summary from local XML/PDF/SI figure captions and Table 1; claims are bounded to assays actually present.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: For SB1 and DJK5, stereorandomization reduces or abolishes antibacterial and EYPG/EYPC vesicle-leakage activity while racemic mixtures retain parent-like activity, supporting a folding-dependent membrane-disruptive phenotype for these alpha-helical AMPs.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: SB1 and DJK5 variants in Table 1
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper supports membrane-disruptive phenotype changes, not a single molecular binding target for antibiofilm activity.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Indolicidin remains active in a disordered conformation context and serves as a control that membrane disruption does not always require alpha-helical folding.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: L-Indo, D-Indo, and sr-Indo Table 1 rows
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is comparative phenotype/mechanism context; exact membrane target is not identified.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: For T25 analogues, stereorandomization can preserve antibacterial/EYPG activity while suppressing EYPC leakage and hemolysis; the homochiral G0/G1 core is implicated in hemolysis and cell toxicity.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: L-T25, D-T25, sr-T25, sr-T25a, and sr-T25b
mechanism_claims.limitations: Exact graph-derived cytotoxicity values from Figure 3/S15 were not digitized; the final claim is qualitative and table-supported for MHC/leakage.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: For PMB2 analogues, stereorandomization suppresses membrane disruption and LPS-neutralizing activity while some antibacterial activity remains, indicating stereochemistry-sensitive membrane/LPS effects and possible additional targets.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: PMB, PMB2, sr-PMB2, sr-PMB2a, and sr-PMB2b
mechanism_claims.limitations: The existence of additional targets is an inference from preserved antibacterial activity without visible membrane damage; the specific target is not identified.
